Update columns in place

Source: R/update.R
zutable-update.Rd

x[, col := expression] writes new values into an existing column, keeping its type: SQL's UPDATE. Several columns are a block, x[, { a := ...; b := ... }], whose statements run in order: name <- value binds a local, and each statement sees the columns and locals as those above it left them. The block is typed as a whole before any data is touched, every new column is computed before any is written, and the commit replaces column pointers, so a failure leaves the table as it was and a vector shared with another object is never changed.

Usage

copy(x)

freeze(x)

is_frozen(x)

Arguments

x

A zutable.

Value

The bracket returns x, invisibly. copy() returns a new zutable; freeze() returns x, invisibly; is_frozen() TRUE or FALSE.

Details

With where, only the matching rows are written, and aggregates are computed over those rows. With by, an aggregate is computed per group and written to the group's rows. Each value is one value, or one per row written.

The table is changed in place: every alias of it sees the update. copy() returns an independent table for one allocation. freeze() marks a table, in place and for good, so that every write route raises a zutable_frozen_error; queries read it as before.

Examples

d <- zutable(id = c(1L, 1L, 2L), px = c(10, 20, 30), qty = c(1L, 2L, 3L),
             notional = NA_real_, share = NA_real_)
d[, {
  w <- px * qty
  notional := w
  share := w / sum(w)
}, by = id]
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 5 columns
#>   id      px        qty     notional  share
#>   <int32> <float64> <int32> <float64> <float64>
#> 1 1       10        1       10        0.2
#> 2 1       20        2       40        0.8
#> 3 2       30        3       90        1.0
d
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 5 columns
#>   id      px        qty     notional  share
#>   <int32> <float64> <int32> <float64> <float64>
#> 1 1       10        1       10        0.2
#> 2 1       20        2       40        0.8
#> 3 2       30        3       90        1.0
freeze(d)
is_frozen(d)
#> [1] TRUE
